Lara (Support): Heads-up — ACME corp is seeing the model return invalid JSON when using our structured_output mode. They hit this in production, ~10% of requests failing parse. Ticket #12345.
Olivia (Customer Success): Ugh. Customer says it breaks downstream ingestion, causing order failures. They want ETA and mitigation. P1 from their side.
Lara (Support): They included a few bad responses and the request_id for one failure: rq_0b9f3a. Attached sample below.
Olivia (Customer Success): Confirm SLA: we promised an initial response within 4 hours, remediation plan within 24. Can we commit to a mitigation in the next 4 hours?
support-bot: Ticket #12345 created, priority=P1, owner=Lara (Support), linked to /incidents/785.
Raj (Eng): Assigning to oncall for quick triage. Can you paste the exact request payload, model, and whether structured_output was strict/relaxed? Also sample failing response.
Lara (Support): Request details they sent:
```
POST /v1/generate
{
  "model": "redwood-instruct-4x",
  "structured_output": "strict",
  "prompt": "Return invoice as JSON using schema X",
  "max_tokens": 350
}
```
And one of the failing responses (customer copy):
```
{"invoice_id": "INV-233","amount": 123.45,"items": [ {"sku": "A1","qty": 2}],, "notes": null}
```
(note the double comma before "notes")
Raj (Eng): Thanks — that double-comma is a clear syntax error. Need to know whether it is deterministic or intermittent. Do they see the error across multiple model versions?
Lara (Support): They saw it across ~3 different requests and reported it starting after a prompt tweak last week. They said it happens with the same prompt ~1 in 10 times.
Nina (Oncall): I'm on it. Reproducing locally now with the exact payload and model. Will run 200 requests to estimate rate.
Raj (Eng): Potential culprits: 1) model hallucinated a stray comma during list rendering; 2) our structured_output post-processing attempted a naive concat and introduced an extra comma when items list empty/has trailing punctuation.
Nina (Oncall): Quick check: logs for rq_0b9f3a show no post-processing exception. Raw model tokens show:
```
... "items": [ { "sku": "A1", "qty": 2 } ], , "notes" : null ...
```
So the token stream itself contained the extra comma.
Raj (Eng): Ok that points to generation, not postprocess. Two immediate workarounds for the customer: 1) switch structured_output from "strict" to "relaxed" (best-effort parser) so malformed outputs are auto-corrected; 2) fallback to text mode then run a robust JSON extractor on the response (regex/json5) before ingestion. Both are temporary.
Olivia (Customer Success): Can we offer a safe automated patch? Customer wants to avoid manual changes.
Raj (Eng): We can enable a gate in the response pipeline to run a quick JSON sanitizer that strips duplicate commas and fixes simple issues before parsing. Low-risk and quick to roll in Dedicated/Hosted. For Private we'd provide a patch.
Lara (Support): Customer asked for a timeline. If we push sanitizer as a runtime toggle, how fast?
Nina (Oncall): I can deploy a Canary sanitizer to the hosted cluster in ~6 hours (dev->canary->prod). If we scope to a strict set of fixes (remove duplicate commas, strip trailing commas in arrays/objects) we can do it safely.
Raj (Eng): Agree. Also need to reduce recurrence: run prompt/eval suite against schema X and add rejection heuristics when generation token sequence is likely to break schema (low-cost): e.g., monitor token-level logits to detect abrupt punctuation duplication. Longer-term: update decoding constraints to prefer valid closures for JSON tokens.
Olivia (Customer Success): I'll relay: initial mitigation (toggle sanitizer) in 6 hours, post-mortem + permanent fix roadmap in 48 hours. Customer needs that in writing.
Lara (Support): Drafting the customer note now. Will include repro steps and suggested temporary client-side fallback (best-effort parser).
support-bot: Assigned to Nina (Oncall). Incident update scheduled in 2 hours.
Nina (Oncall): Repro results: 200 runs -> 18 failed parses (~9%). Attached minimal repro script:
```
# python pseudocode
for i in range(200):
  resp = client.generate(model="redwood-instruct-4x", structured_output="strict", prompt=prompt)
  try:
    json.loads(resp.text)
  except Exception as e:
    failures += 1
print(failures)
```
Failure pattern: extra punctuation or missing quotes in ~70% of failing cases, trailing commas in remainder.
Raj (Eng): Thanks. Action items: 1) Nina: roll sanitizer canary to hosted cluster (ETA 6h). 2) Raj: drafting decoding constraint PR to reduce punctuation duplication (ETA 48h). 3) Lara/Olivia: send customer mitigation + ETA email now.
Olivia (Customer Success): Sending now. Email excerpt: "We're seeing intermittent malformed JSON in structured_output mode. Short-term: we will enable an automated sanitizer in our hosted runtime within 6 hours to avoid ingestion failures. We'll follow up with a permanent fix in 48 hours. We recommend a client-side tolerant parser in the meantime."
Lara (Support): Customer acknowledged and downgraded immediate escalation urgency but still wants follow-up.
Nina (Oncall): Canary started: hitting canary endpoint for same prompt shows failure rate down to ~1.5% for 500 runs. Deploying to prod next if no regressions in 1 hour.
Raj (Eng): Great. After prod deploy, we'll keep sampling and add a regression alert on schema X to detect any reintroduction.
Olivia (Customer Success): I'll set a check-in with ACME in 24h. Thanks team. :thumbsup:
Lara (Support): Closing internal P1; will reopen if sanitizer causes false positives.
Nina (Oncall): Prod deploy complete. Monitoring looks good so far.
Raj (Eng): Follow-up plan: merge PR for decoding constraints and add structured_output regression tests to CI. ETA 48h.
Olivia (Customer Success): Noted. I'll pass on the 48h roadmap and plan the post-mortem.
Lara (Support): Filed postmortem template and linked incident. Ticket updated.
Nina (Oncall): Leaving notes in incident: root cause likely model tokenization/decoding edge-case. Permanent fix involves decoding constraints + better evals.
Olivia (Customer Success): Thanks everyone. Customer is relieved by the canary results. We'll close the support case after 48h verification. :tada:
